FAQs About Our Physiotherapy​​ Service in Milton

Do I need a doctor's referral to start physiotherapy? No, a doctor's referral isn't required to begin physiotherapy at Tonic Physiotherapy & Rehabilitation Centre. You can book an appointment directly. However, some insurance plans may require a referral for reimbursement, so it's advisable to check with your provider. What should I expect during my first physiotherapy session? Your initial visit will involve a comprehensive assessment, including a discussion of your medical history and a physical examination to identify movement patterns and areas of concern. Based on this evaluation, we'll develop a personalized treatment plan tailored to your needs. How long are the physiotherapy sessions? The first assessment typically lasts about 60 minutes, while follow-up sessions are approximately 30 minutes. Each session is one-on-one with your physiotherapist to ensure focused and individualized care. What conditions can physiotherapy help with? Physiotherapy can help with a wide range of conditions, including back and neck pain, sports injuries, arthritis, joint and muscle problems, post-surgical recovery, and neurological conditions like stroke or Parkinson’s disease. It’s also effective for treating work and motor vehicle injuries, balance issues, and chronic pain. Physiotherapists assess the root cause of your symptoms and create a personalized treatment plan to restore movement and improve function. Is physiotherapy covered by insurance? Yes, most private insurance plans cover physiotherapy, but coverage amounts and requirements vary. Check with your provider for details. What should I wear to my physiotherapy appointment? You should wear loose, comfortable clothing that allows easy movement and provides access to the area being treated. For example, wear shorts for knee or hip issues and a tank top or t-shirt for shoulder or upper back concerns. Athletic wear is ideal. Proper footwear, like running shoes, may also be helpful if your session includes exercises. Will I get an exercise program? Yes, most physiotherapy treatment plans include a personalized exercise program. These exercises are designed to support your recovery, improve strength, flexibility, and mobility, and prevent future injuries. Your physiotherapist will demonstrate each exercise, ensure you perform them correctly, and adjust the program as you progress. You’ll typically be asked to continue the exercises at home between sessions for the best results. How is my progress measured? Your physiotherapist will measure your progress through regular assessments of your pain levels, range of motion, strength, and functional abilities. They may use tools like goniometers, strength tests, or patient-reported outcome measures. Progress is also tracked by your ability to perform daily activities, meet treatment goals, and reduce reliance on medication or mobility aids. Treatment plans are adjusted based on these results to ensure consistent improvement. What is physiotherapy? Physiotherapy is a treatment method that uses movement, targeted exercises, manual therapy, and physical techniques to relieve pain, restore mobility, and improve overall physical function. It helps people recover from injuries, manage chronic conditions, and regain strength and flexibility without surgery or medication. Do I need a referral to see a physiotherapist in Milton, Ontario? No, Ontario grants "direct access," meaning most physiotherapy clinics accept patients without a doctor’s note. However, check your extended health insurance, as some insurers may require a referral for reimbursement. Does OHIP or private insurance cover physiotherapy in Milton, Ontario? Ontario Health Insurance (OHIP) only covers physiotherapy for clients recovering from joint replacement surgery, hip/knee fractures, or major orthopedic procedures. Most extended/private health plans do cover physiotherapy; to be safe, check your policy or call your insurer. What do I need to bring to my first physiotherapy appointment? Wear comfortable clothing (e.g. shorts and t‑shirt) for access to the treated area.
  • Bring any relevant medical reports, imaging (e.g. X‑ray/MRI), insurance or benefits card, and auto/work‑injury claim info if applicable.
  • Arrive ~15 minutes early to complete intake paperwork.
What happens at my first physiotherapy session? A 30–60 minute comprehensive assessment: history review, physical examination (range of motion, posture, strength). Based on findings, the therapist will explain the diagnosis, set goals, and design a personalized treatment plan. What conditions can a physiotherapist treat in Milton? These include (but aren’t limited to):
  • Back, neck, shoulder, hip, knee, ankle, wrist pain
  • Sports injuries, post-surgical rehabilitation (e.g. total joint replacement)
  • Motor vehicle accident (MVA) and workplace injuries
  • Dizziness/vertigo, pelvic floor and pregnancy-related pain, arthritis, chronic pain, TMJ dysfunction (Common conditions across Milton clinics)

","_id":"ba2b631"},{"acc_title":"What conditions can physiotherapy help with?","acc_content":"

Physiotherapy can help with a wide range of conditions, including back and neck pain, sports injuries, arthritis, joint and muscle problems, post-surgical recovery, and neurological conditions like stroke or Parkinson’s disease. It’s also effective for treating work and motor vehicle injuries, balance issues, and chronic pain. Physiotherapists assess the root cause of your symptoms and create a personalized treatment plan to restore movement and improve function.

You should wear loose, comfortable clothing that allows easy movement and provides access to the area being treated. Proper footwear, like running shoes, may also be helpful if your session includes exercises.

"},{"_id":"a654c35","acc_title":"Will I get an exercise program?","acc_content":"

Yes, most physiotherapy treatment plans include a personalized exercise program. These exercises are designed to support your recovery, improve strength, flexibility, and mobility, and prevent future injuries. Your physiotherapist will demonstrate each exercise, ensure you perform them correctly, and adjust the program as you progress. You’ll typically be asked to continue the exercises at home between sessions for the best results.

"},{"_id":"efd43d5","acc_title":"How is my progress measured?","acc_content":"

Your physiotherapist will measure your progress through regular assessments of your pain levels, range of motion, strength, and functional abilities. They may use tools like goniometers, strength tests, or patient-reported outcome measures. Progress is also tracked by your ability to perform daily activities, meet treatment goals, and reduce reliance on medication or mobility aids. Treatment plans are adjusted based on these results to ensure consistent improvement.

"},{"acc_title":"What is physiotherapy?","acc_content":"

Physiotherapy is a treatment method that uses movement, targeted exercises, manual therapy, and physical techniques to relieve pain, restore mobility, and improve overall physical function.
